title: Typical or forced: how special the universal couplings of one body are

key_results.statement: Class $\mathcal C^+$ (one Model D body, sharp linear field $N(x)=n_1x$, $n_1\neq0$, weak records): $mg_m=n_1\alpha_0$, $g_\eta=n_1\alpha_1$, $\mathcal F=\mathcal F_{\rm rec}-n_1\beta_0$, $\mathcal F_1=-n_1\beta_1$, $\mathcal F_{\rm rec}=-\kappa\langle X\rangle$; the map onto $\boldsymbol g\in\mathbb R^5$ is a bijection at fixed $\mathcal F_{\rm rec}$, so every $\boldsymbol g$ is admissible.

In $\mathcal C^+$, first order in the gradients, from rest: $a_{k,\sigma}(0)=\tau^2(\sigma\mathcal F_1-g_\eta)+\tau^2\frac{m}{M_k}\ell_\sigma$ with $\ell_\sigma=\sigma\mathcal F/m-g_m+g_\eta-\sigma\mathcal F_1$.

For every $N\ge2$: the fall from rest is level-independent on branch $\sigma$ iff $\ell_\sigma=0$ (value $\tau^2(\sigma\mathcal F_1-g_\eta)$); on both branches iff $g_m=g_\eta$, $\mathcal F=m\mathcal F_1$; on both with $a_+=a_-$ iff also $\mathcal F_1=0$; codimensions 1, 1, 2, 3 in $\mathbb R^5$.

Upper branch through $v^2$ exactly: $N=2$: $\ell_+=0$ and $\Delta=4a_+M_0M_1(M_0+M_1)/\tau^4$ (codim 2); $N\ge3$: $g_m=g_\eta=\mathcal F_1$, $\mathcal F=mg_\eta$ (codim 3, $a_+=0$); at leading order in $M_k/\tau$: $\mathcal U_4^{\pm}$ (codim 2); lower branch by $(\mathcal F,\mathcal F_1)\mapsto-(\mathcal F,\mathcal F_1)$; both branches exactly: only $g_\zeta$ free (codim 4, zero fall).

Rate at $x_0$ in $\mathcal C^+$ (frozen coefficients at $x_0$, then $W\to\infty$; zeroth order in the gradients): $r(x_0)=[1+(g_\eta-\mathcal F_1)x_0]/\lambda_0=\frac{N}{2\pi}(E^+_{x_0,k+1}-E^+_{x_0,k})$ for every $k$.

First equality of (4.24) in $\mathcal C^+$: for a branch start on level $k$ with $a_{k,+}(0)\neq0$, $\frac{d^2\bar x}{d\lambda^2}|_{\rm drift}=d_0a_{k,+}(0)\hat e$, at first order in the gradients and with weak records (reduction to a member of $\mathcal C$ with the same level-$k$ block).

Defect of the label form of (4.24) on level $k$: $\mathcal D_k=\tau^2\frac{m}{M_k}\ell_+ +O(\lVert\boldsymbol g\rVert^2)$; (4.24) holds on one level iff on all iff $\ell_+=0$; $\mathcal U_5=\mathcal U_4^+\setminus\{\mathcal F_1=g_\eta\}$, dimension 4, codimension 1, every $N\ge2$; on $\mathcal U_5$ the label form is equivalent to (4.24) by (17.13).

At distance $\delta$ from $\mathcal U_4^+$ (Euclidean norm of $(g_m,g_\eta,\mathcal F/m,\mathcal F_1,g_\zeta)$): $\max|a_{k,+}(0)-a_{k',+}(0)|=2\tau^2\delta\,d_{N-1}/(m+d_{N-1})$ and $\max_k|\mathcal D_k|=2\tau^2\delta$, both of first order in $\delta$.

Relistings $C_{\rm own}\to C_{\rm own}-Q$, $C_\gamma\to C_\gamma+Q\otimes\mathbb 1$ (M1: constant into the record term; M2: $\epsilon\sigma_3$ into the record term; M3: $\Phi_x\to\Phi_x-c$; M4: constant into the field pair term; M5: on-site $\epsilon\sigma_1$ from the record term to the own term); the effective level blocks up to a common constant, $\boldsymbol g$ and all sets are invariant.

R1 and R2$_{\rm c}$ (R2 with one common factor) are not M6-well-defined (M2 switches their verdict for fixed $C$; M1 for R1; M4, M5 for R2$_{\rm c}$); in the setting's listing both give $g_m=g_\eta$, $\mathcal F_1=0$, $\mathcal F=\mathcal F_{\rm rec}$, not necessary for $\mathcal U_4^{\pm}$ or $\mathcal U_5$, sufficient for $\mathcal U_4^{\pm}$ iff $\mathcal F_{\rm rec}=0$ (with $\alpha\neq0$ for $\mathcal U_5$ iff $\mathcal F_{\rm rec}=0$); controls: $\mathcal F_{\rm rec}\neq0$, or $G'=\alpha\sigma_3\otimes((m-\epsilon)\mathbb 1_N+D)$ in listing M2.

R2 as written (a factor $c_k$ on every level, not necessarily common) is not M6-well-defined (M4, M5 switch its verdict; invariant under M1, M2); in the setting's listing it is $\mathcal F_1=0$, $\mathcal F=\mathcal F_{\rm rec}$ (codim 2), neither necessary nor sufficient for $\mathcal U_4^{\pm}$, $\mathcal U_4^+$ or $\mathcal U_5$ for every $\mathcal F_{\rm rec}$; control: $G=\epsilon\sigma_3\otimes D$, $\epsilon\neq0$, $n_1\epsilon\neq\pm\mathcal F_{\rm rec}/m$, fails item 4 on both branches.

R3 ($B_{x+1,k}-B_{x,k}=M_k\Gamma$ with level-independent $\Gamma$ on the branch label) is well defined and equivalent to $\mathcal U_4^{\pm}$; $\Gamma$ traceless iff $\mathcal U_4^{=}$; R3$^+$ iff $\mathcal U_4^+$, with $\gamma_+\neq0$ iff $\mathcal U_5$; no control from rest; through $v^2$ exactly R3 with $a_+\neq0$ fails.

Verdict in $\mathcal C^+$ at first order in the gradients: all sets have empty interior and positive codimension (exceptional, not typical), are broken at first order in $\delta$, are selected by R3, and are not enforced by the language since every $\boldsymbol g$ is admissible.

open_issues: (17.13) uses that the first equality of (4.24), quoted per level k, depends only on the block of the start's level; this is read from the quoted form, not re-checked in 04-branch-fall.

(17.6) is the frozen-coefficient, W→∞ form only; the finite-W rate, its bound in (3.23), and the error of the frozen rate as an approximation to readings of the actual inhomogeneous evolution are not derived for F1 ≠ 0.
The lower branch through v² uses (4.17) at σ = −1 level by level, in the form analogous to (4.20), which is quoted for the upper branch only.
F_rec = −κ⟨X⟩ depends on the medium background; whether the background of 03-ilang-space fixes ⟨X⟩ = 0 is not quoted.
R3 is equivalent to the property it selects; whether a requirement outside C+ selects it (branch- or level-mixing couplings, non-linear profiles, non-sharp fields, several bodies) is out of scope.
